37:     agent_msg_t  items[AGENT_BUS_QUEUE_LEN];
38:     int             head;
39:     int             tail;
40:     int             count;
41:     pthread_mutex_t lock;
42:     pthread_cond_t  not_empty;
43:     pthread_cond_t  not_full;
44: } msg_queue_t;
45: 
46: /* -- Private Data --------------------------------------------------------- */
47: 
48: static msg_queue_t g_inbound_queue;
49: static msg_queue_t g_outbound_queue;
50: static bool g_initialized = false;
51: static volatile bool g_bus_shutdown = false;
52: 
53: /* -- Private Functions ---------------------------------------------------- */
54: 
55: static void msg_queue_init(msg_queue_t *queue)
56: {
57:     memset(queue, 0, sizeof(*queue));
58:     pthread_mutex_init(&queue->lock, NULL);
59:     pthread_cond_init(&queue->not_empty, NULL);
60:     pthread_cond_init(&queue->not_full, NULL);
61: }
62: 
63: static void msg_queue_destroy(msg_queue_t *queue)
64: {
65:     pthread_mutex_destroy(&queue->lock);
66:     pthread_cond_destroy(&queue->not_empty);
67:     pthread_cond_destroy(&queue->not_full);
68:     memset(queue, 0, sizeof(*queue));
69: }
70: 
71: static int msg_queue_push(msg_queue_t *queue, const agent_msg_t *msg,
72:                           uint32_t timeout_ms)
73: {
74:     struct timespec ts;
75: 
76:     pthread_mutex_lock(&queue->lock);
77: 
78:     if (queue->count >= AGENT_BUS_QUEUE_LEN) {
79:         if (timeout_ms == 0) {
80:             pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue->lock);
81:             return ERROR;
82:         }
83: 
84:         clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);
85:         ts.tv_sec += (time_t)(timeout_ms / 1000);
86:         ts.tv_nsec += (long)((timeout_ms % 1000) * 1000000L);
87:         if (ts.tv_nsec >= 1000000000L) {
88:             ts.tv_sec++;
89:             ts.tv_nsec -= 1000000000L;
90:         }
91: 
92:         /* Wait for space */
93:         while (queue->count >= AGENT_BUS_QUEUE_LEN) {
94:             if (pthread_cond_timedwait(&queue->not_full, &queue->lock, &ts) != 0) {
95:                 pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue->lock);
96:                 syslog(LOG_WARNING, "[%s] Queue full, dropping message\n", TAG);
97:                 return ERROR;
98:             }
99:         }
100:     }
101: 
102:     queue->items[queue->tail] = *msg;
103:     queue->tail = (queue->tail + 1) % AGENT_BUS_QUEUE_LEN;
104:     queue->count++;
105: 
106:     pthread_cond_signal(&queue->not_empty);
107:     pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue->lock);
108:     return OK;
109: }
110: 
111: static int msg_queue_pop(msg_queue_t *queue, agent_msg_t *msg,
112:                          uint32_t timeout_ms)
113: {
114:     struct timespec ts;
115: 
116:     pthread_mutex_lock(&queue->lock);
117: 
118:     while (queue->count == 0) {
119:         if (g_bus_shutdown) {
120:             pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue->lock);
121:             return ERROR;
122:         }
123:         if (timeout_ms == UINT32_MAX) {
124:             pthread_cond_wait(&queue->not_empty, &queue->lock);
125:         } else {
126:             clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);
127:             ts.tv_sec += (time_t)(timeout_ms / 1000);
128:             ts.tv_nsec += (long)((timeout_ms % 1000) * 1000000L);
129:             if (ts.tv_nsec >= 1000000000L) {
130:                 ts.tv_sec++;
131:                 ts.tv_nsec -= 1000000000L;
132:             }
133: 
134:             if (pthread_cond_timedwait(&queue->not_empty, &queue->lock, &ts) != 0) {
135:                 pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue->lock);
136:                 return ERROR;
137:             }
138:         }
139:     }
140: 
141:     *msg = queue->items[queue->head];
142:     queue->head = (queue->head + 1) % AGENT_BUS_QUEUE_LEN;
143:     queue->count--;
144: 
145:     pthread_cond_signal(&queue->not_full);
146:     pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue->lock);
147:     return OK;
148: }

173:     }

175:     msg_queue_init(&g_inbound_queue);
176:     msg_queue_init(&g_outbound_queue);
177:     g_bus_shutdown = false;
178:     g_initialized = true;
179: 
180:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[%s] Message bus initialized (depth %d)\n",
181:            TAG, AGENT_BUS_QUEUE_LEN);

23: /**
24:  * message_bus_tap.c — outbound message tap mechanism
25:  *
26:  * A lightweight per-channel intercept for outbound messages.
27:  * Used by the integration test harness to capture agent responses
28:  * without interfering with normal channel dispatch.
29:  *
30:  * Max 4 concurrent taps.  When no taps are registered the overhead
31:  * is a single mutex lock/unlock per outbound message.
32:  */
33: 
34: #include "core/message_bus_tap.h"
35: 
36: #include <pthread.h>
37: #include <string.h>
38: #include <syslog.h>
39: 
40: #define TAP_MAX_SLOTS 4
41: 
42: typedef struct {
43:     char channel[16];
44:     mbus_tap_cb_t cb;
45:     void* cookie;
46:     bool active;
47: } tap_slot_t;
48: 
49: static tap_slot_t g_taps[TAP_MAX_SLOTS];
50: static pthread_mutex_t g_tap_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
51: 
52: int mbus_tap_register(const char* channel, mbus_tap_cb_t cb, void* cookie)
53: {
54:     if (!channel || !cb) {
55:         return ERROR;
56:     }
57: 
58:     pthread_mutex_lock(&g_tap_lock);
59: 
60:     /* Check for duplicate */
61:     for (int i = 0; i < TAP_MAX_SLOTS; i++) {
62:         if (g_taps[i].active && strcmp(g_taps[i].channel, channel) == 0) {
63:             pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_tap_lock);
64:             syslog(LOG_WARNING, "[tap] channel '%s' already tapped\n", channel);
65:             return ERROR;
66:         }
67:     }
68: 
69:     /* Find free slot */
70:     for (int i = 0; i < TAP_MAX_SLOTS; i++) {
71:         if (!g_taps[i].active) {
72:             strncpy(g_taps[i].channel, channel, sizeof(g_taps[i].channel) - 1);
73:             g_taps[i].channel[sizeof(g_taps[i].channel) - 1] = '\0';
74:             g_taps[i].cb = cb;
75:             g_taps[i].cookie = cookie;
76:             g_taps[i].active = true;
77:             pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_tap_lock);
78:             syslog(LOG_INFO, "[tap] registered tap for channel '%s'\n", channel);
79:             return OK;
80:         }
81:     }
82: 
83:     pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_tap_lock);
84:     syslog(LOG_WARNING, "[tap] no free slots (max %d)\n", TAP_MAX_SLOTS);
85:     return ERROR;
86: }
87: 
88: void mbus_tap_unregister(const char* channel)
89: {
90:     if (!channel) {
91:         return;
92:     }
93: 
94:     pthread_mutex_lock(&g_tap_lock);
95: 
96:     for (int i = 0; i < TAP_MAX_SLOTS; i++) {
97:         if (g_taps[i].active && strcmp(g_taps[i].channel, channel) == 0) {
98:             g_taps[i].active = false;
99:             g_taps[i].cb = NULL;
100:             g_taps[i].cookie = NULL;
101:             syslog(LOG_INFO, "[tap] unregistered tap for channel '%s'\n", channel);
102:             break;
103:         }
104:     }
105: 
106:     pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_tap_lock);
107: }
108: 
109: bool mbus_tap_try_deliver(const agent_msg_t* msg)
110: {
111:     if (!msg || !msg->channel[0]) {
112:         return false;
113:     }
114: 
115:     pthread_mutex_lock(&g_tap_lock);
116: 
117:     for (int i = 0; i < TAP_MAX_SLOTS; i++) {
118:         if (g_taps[i].active && strcmp(g_taps[i].channel, msg->channel) == 0) {
119:             mbus_tap_cb_t cb = g_taps[i].cb;
120:             void* cookie = g_taps[i].cookie;
121:             pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_tap_lock);
122: 
123:             /* Invoke callback outside the lock to avoid deadlock */
124:             cb(msg, cookie);
125:             return true;
126:         }
127:     }
128: 
129:     pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_tap_lock);
130:     return false;
131: }

119: /* Heap-allocated payload passed to lv_async_call so the LVGL thread
120:  * can safely create widgets without cross-thread invalidation.
121:  * Freed by the async callback after use. */
122: typedef struct {
123:     char text[LVGL_UI_MSG_MAX_LEN];
124:     bool is_user;
125: } async_msg_t;

140: /* ── Ring buffer ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */

142: /**
143:  * Add a message to the chat history ring buffer.
144:  *
145:  * When count < CHAT_HISTORY_MAX, writes at head and increments count.
146:  * When count == CHAT_HISTORY_MAX, overwrites the oldest message and
147:  * deletes its LVGL bubble widget if present.
148:  *
149:  * Text is truncated to LVGL_UI_MSG_MAX_LEN - 1 bytes with explicit
150:  * NUL termination (rule coding-9).
151:  *
152:  * Returns pointer to the newly written slot (inside the ring buffer,
153:  * no stack allocation of chat_msg_t — rule coding-6).
154:  */
155: static chat_msg_t* chat_history_add(chat_history_t* h, const char* text, bool is_user)
156: {
157:     chat_msg_t* slot = &h->msgs[h->head];
158: 
159:     /* When buffer is full, recycle the oldest slot */
160:     if (h->count == CHAT_HISTORY_MAX) {
161:         if (slot->bubble) {
162:             lv_obj_del(slot->bubble);
163:             slot->bubble = NULL;
164:         }
165:     } else {
166:         h->count++;
167:     }
168: 
169:     /* Write message text with truncation (coding-9: strncpy + manual NUL) */
170:     strncpy(slot->text, text, LVGL_UI_MSG_MAX_LEN - 1);
171:     slot->text[LVGL_UI_MSG_MAX_LEN - 1] = '\0';
172: 
173:     slot->is_user = is_user;
174:     slot->bubble = NULL;
175: 
176:     h->head = (h->head + 1) % CHAT_HISTORY_MAX;
177: 
178:     return slot;
179: }

200:      * already has one.  Creating a second display causes resource

377: /* Semaphore for synchronizing async stop with LVGL thread */
378: static sem_t s_stop_sem;
379: 
380: /* Internal cleanup — must be called from LVGL thread context */
381: static void lvgl_ui_do_cleanup(void)
382: {
383:     int i;
384: 
385:     if (s_state.screen) {
386:         /* If our screen is the active screen, restore the previous
387:          * (launcher) screen first.  Deleting the active screen without
388:          * loading another one leaves LVGL with no valid screen — the
389:          * next lv_timer_handler() call crashes with a MemManage fault
390:          * (NULL pointer dereference at offset 0x32 in lv_obj_t). */
391:         if (s_state.screen_visible && s_state.prev_screen) {
392:             lv_screen_load(s_state.prev_screen);
393:         }
394: 
395:         lv_obj_del(s_state.screen);
396:         s_state.screen = NULL;
397:     }
398: 
399:     s_state.screen_visible = false;
400:     s_state.prev_screen = NULL;
401: 
402:     if (s_state.font) {
403:         vg_font_destroy(s_state.font);
404:         s_state.font = NULL;
405:     }
406: 
407:     s_state.chat_list = NULL;
408:     s_state.ptt_btn = NULL;
409:     s_state.ptt_label = NULL;
410:     s_state.rec_indicator = NULL;
411:     s_state.close_btn = NULL;
412: 
413:     for (i = 0; i < CHAT_HISTORY_MAX; i++) {
414:         s_state.history.msgs[i].bubble = NULL;
415:     }
416: 
417:     s_state.history.head = 0;
418:     s_state.history.count = 0;
419: }

421: static void stop_screen_async_cb(void* data)
422: {
423:     (void)data;
424: 
425:     lvgl_ui_do_cleanup();
426:     sem_post(&s_stop_sem);
427: }

429: /* Stop from within the LVGL thread (e.g. close button callback).
430:  * Performs cleanup directly — no async scheduling needed. */
431: void lvgl_ui_channel_stop_sync(void)
432: {
433:     if (!s_state.initialized || !s_state.running) {
434:         return;
435:     }
436: 
437:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[%s] stopping (sync)\n", TAG);
438: 
439:     s_state.running = false;
440:     lvgl_ui_do_cleanup();
441:     pthread_mutex_destroy(&s_state.lock);
442:     s_state.initialized = false;
443: 
444:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[%s] stopped\n", TAG);
445: }

447: /* Stop from an external thread (e.g. velaquit shutdown).
448:  * Schedules cleanup in the LVGL thread to avoid racing with the
449:  * miwear/launcher event loop. */
450: void lvgl_ui_channel_stop(void)
451: {
452:     /* No-op if not initialized or not running */
453:     if (!s_state.initialized || !s_state.running) {
454:         return;
455:     }
456: 
457:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[%s] stopping\n", TAG);
458: 
459:     /* Mark as not running first — prevents callbacks (PTT, close_btn,
460:      * chat_view_add_message) from touching widgets during teardown. */
461:     s_state.running = false;
462: 
463:     /* Schedule cleanup in the LVGL thread to avoid racing with the
464:      * miwear/launcher event loop.  Direct lv_obj_del from the
465:      * shutdown thread causes a MemManage fault because the LVGL
466:      * thread may be mid-render on the same objects. */
467:     sem_init(&s_stop_sem, 0, 0);
468:     lv_async_call(stop_screen_async_cb, NULL);
469: 
470:     /* Wait for LVGL thread to complete the deletion (timeout 2s) */
471:     struct timespec ts;
472: 
473:     clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts);
474:     ts.tv_sec += 2;
475: 
476:     if (sem_timedwait(&s_stop_sem, &ts) != 0) {
477:         syslog(LOG_WARNING,
478:             "[%s] async stop timed out, forcing cleanup\n", TAG);
479:         /* Fallback: NULL out pointers without deleting (leak is
480:          * acceptable during shutdown to avoid crash). */
481:         s_state.screen = NULL;
482:         s_state.chat_list = NULL;
483:         s_state.ptt_btn = NULL;
484:         s_state.ptt_label = NULL;
485:         s_state.rec_indicator = NULL;
486:         s_state.close_btn = NULL;
487:     }
488: 
489:     sem_destroy(&s_stop_sem);
490: 
491:     /* Destroy the mutex */
492:     pthread_mutex_destroy(&s_state.lock);
493: 
494:     s_state.initialized = false;
495: 
496:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[%s] stopped\n", TAG);
497: }

499: /* Async callback: load screen inside LVGL thread context */
500: static void show_screen_async_cb(void* data)
501: {
502:     (void)data;
503:     if (!s_state.initialized || !s_state.running || !s_state.screen) {
504:         return;
505:     }
506:     if (s_state.screen_visible) {
507:         return;
508:     }
509: 
510:     /* Create CJK font here — inside the LVGL thread — so the
511:      * FreeType size handle is owned by the same thread that will
512:      * later rasterize glyphs.  Creating it from the main thread
513:      * (in init) causes FT_Err_Invalid_Size_Handle (0x55). */
514:     if (!s_state.font) {
515:         s_state.font = vg_font_create("MiSans-Medium", 18,
516:             LV_FREETYPE_FONT_STYLE_NORMAL);
517:         if (s_state.font) {
518:             lv_obj_set_style_text_font(s_state.screen, s_state.font, 0);
519:         } else {
520:             syslog(LOG_WARNING, "[%s] vg_font_create failed, keeping montserrat\n", TAG);
521:         }
522:     }
523: 
524:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[%s] loading chat screen\n", TAG);
525: 
526:     /* Save the current screen so we can restore it on stop.
527:      * The launcher (miwear) owns this screen — we must not delete it. */
528:     s_state.prev_screen = lv_screen_active();
529: 
530:     lv_screen_load(s_state.screen);
531:     s_state.screen_visible = true;
532: }

550: int lvgl_ui_channel_send(const char* text)
551: {
552:     int ret;
553:     async_msg_t* payload;
554: 
555:     /* Parameter validation: NULL or empty string */
556:     if (!text || text[0] == '\0') {
557:         syslog(LOG_ERR, "[%s] send: invalid text (NULL or empty)\n", TAG);
558:         return -EINVAL;
559:     }
560: 
561:     /* Check channel readiness */
562:     if (!s_state.initialized || !s_state.running) {
563:         syslog(LOG_ERR, "[%s] send: channel not ready (init=%d run=%d)\n",
564:             TAG, s_state.initialized, s_state.running);
565:         return -EINVAL;
566:     }
567: 
568:     /* Auto-show chat screen on first Agent reply */
569:     if (!s_state.screen_visible) {
570:         lvgl_ui_channel_show();
571:     }
572: 
573:     /* Schedule bubble creation in LVGL thread via lv_async_call.
574:      * This avoids the "Invalidate area is not allowed during rendering"
575:      * assertion crash that occurs when we create LVGL widgets from
576:      * the agent dispatch thread while miwear's LVGL thread is
577:      * mid-render. */
578:     payload = malloc(sizeof(async_msg_t));
579:     if (!payload) {
580:         syslog(LOG_ERR, "[%s] send: async payload alloc failed\n", TAG);
581:         return -ENOMEM;
582:     }
583: 
584:     strncpy(payload->text, text, LVGL_UI_MSG_MAX_LEN - 1);
585:     payload->text[LVGL_UI_MSG_MAX_LEN - 1] = '\0';
586:     payload->is_user = false;
587: 
588:     lv_async_call(chat_view_add_message_async_cb, payload);
589: 
590:     /* TTS is blocking — run after scheduling the UI update */
591:     ret = voice_channel_speak(text);
592:     if (ret != 0) {
593:         syslog(LOG_ERR, "[%s] voice_channel_speak failed (rc=%d)\n", TAG, ret);
594:     }
595: 
596:     return 0;
597: }

599: /* ── Async callback for LVGL thread ────────────────────────── */
600: 
601: /* Called by lv_timer_handler() inside the LVGL thread.
602:  * Safe to create/modify LVGL objects here. */
603: static void chat_view_add_message_async_cb(void* data)
604: {
605:     async_msg_t* payload = (async_msg_t*)data;
606: 
607:     if (!payload) {
608:         return;
609:     }
610: 
611:     if (!s_state.initialized || !s_state.running) {
612:         free(payload);
613:         return;
614:     }
615: 
616:     chat_view_add_message(payload->text, payload->is_user);
617:     free(payload);
618:     payload = NULL;
619: }

623: static void chat_view_add_message(const char* text, bool is_user)
624: {
625:     chat_history_t* h = &s_state.history;
626:     chat_msg_t* slot;
627:     lv_obj_t* bubble;
628:     lv_obj_t* lbl;
629: 
630:     /* If history is already full, trim before overwriting */
631:     if (h->count == CHAT_HISTORY_MAX) {
632:         chat_view_trim_history();
633:     }
634: 
635:     /* Store message in ring buffer (handles truncation + old bubble deletion) */
636:     slot = chat_history_add(h, text, is_user);
637: 
638:     /* Create bubble container inside chat_list */
639:     bubble = lv_obj_create(s_state.chat_list);
640:     if (!bubble) {
641:         syslog(LOG_ERR, "[%s] bubble create failed\n", TAG);
642:         return;
643:     }
644: 
645:     lv_obj_set_width(bubble, lv_pct(85));
646:     lv_obj_set_height(bubble, LV_SIZE_CONTENT);
647:     lv_obj_set_style_radius(bubble, LVGL_UI_BUBBLE_RADIUS, 0);
648:     lv_obj_set_style_pad_all(bubble, LVGL_UI_BUBBLE_PAD, 0);
649:     lv_obj_set_style_border_width(bubble, 0, 0);
650: 
651:     if (is_user) {
652:         /* User bubble: right-aligned, blue background, white text */
653:         lv_obj_set_style_align(bubble, LV_ALIGN_RIGHT_MID, 0);
654:         lv_obj_set_style_bg_color(bubble, lv_color_hex(0x3a7bd5), 0);
655:         lv_obj_set_style_text_color(bubble, lv_color_white(), 0);

1: # 接入通道
2: 
3: AI Agent 支持多种接入通道，所有通道通过 message_bus 统一接入 Agent。
4: 
5: ## CLI
6: 
7: NSH shell 直接输入 `ask <text>` 对话。详见 [CLI 命令参考](cli.md)。
8: 
9: ## 飞书 Bot
10: 
11: WebSocket 长连接，支持群聊/私聊。
12: 
13: ### 配置
14: 
15: ```bash
16: vela> set_feishu_app <app_id> <app_secret>
17: ```
18: 
19: ### 使用示例
20: 
21: 配置好飞书凭证后，直接在飞书群聊或私聊中发消息：
22: 
23: ```
24: 用户: 帮我查询当前系统内存用了多少
25: Bot:  当前系统内存情况：
26:       MemTotal: 8192 KB
27:       MemFree:  3456 KB
28:       已使用约 58%
29: ```
30: 
31: Agent 会自动调用 `run_shell` 工具执行 `cat /proc/meminfo` 并解析结果。
32: 
33: ## WebSocket Server
34: 
35: 端口 28789，支持外部客户端接入。同时用于 Hub 模式接受 Node 连接。
36: 
37: ## MQTT Channel
38: 
39: 通过 MQTT 协议接入，适用于 IoT 设备集成。基于 MQTT-C 库。
40: 
41: ### 配置
42: 
43: ```bash
44: vela> set_mqtt <broker-host>:1883
45: ```
46: 
47: ### 使用示例
48: 
49: ```bash
50: # 在主机上订阅回复 topic
51: mosquitto_sub -h <broker-host> -t "agent/out" -v
52: 
53: # 在主机上发送消息
54: mosquitto_pub -h <broker-host> -t "agent/in" \
55:   -m '{"type":"message","content":"现在几点了？","chat_id":"device1"}'
56: ```
57: 
58: 消息格式（JSON）：
59: - 输入 `agent/in`：`{"type":"message","content":"<文本>","chat_id":"<ID>"}`
60: - 输出 `agent/out`：`{"type":"response","content":"<回复>","chat_id":"<ID>"}`
61: 
62: ## Voice Channel（语音通路）
63: 
64: 通用 ASR/TTS 后端抽象，支持多厂商切换。内置火山引擎后端。
65: 
66: ```
67: Mic → PCM → ASR → text → message_bus → agent_loop
68:                                           ↓
69: Speaker ← PCM ← TTS ← text ← message_bus (outbound)
70: ```
71: 
72: ### 配置
73: 
74: ```bash
75: # 1. 设置 TTS API Key
76: vela> set_volc_key <api_key>
77: 
78: # 2. 设置 ASR 凭证
79: vela> set_volc_asr <app_id> <token> <cluster>
80: 
81: # 3. 可选：设置 TTS 语音角色（默认 zh_male_beijingxiaoye_emo_v2_mars_bigtts）
82: vela> set_volc_speaker zh_male_chunhou
83: 
84: # 4. 切换后端（添加新后端后可用）
85: vela> set_voice_tts volcengine
86: vela> set_voice_asr volcengine
87: ```
88: 
89: ### 测试（QEMU 文件模式）
90: 
91: QEMU 环境下无真实音频硬件，使用文件模式测试：
92: 
93: ```bash
94: # TTS：文本合成为 PCM 文件
95: vela> voice_test_tts 你好世界
96: # TTS OK: 32000 bytes -> /data/agent/tts_out.pcm
97: 
98: # ASR：PCM 文件识别为文本，自动发送给 Agent
99: vela> voice_test_asr /data/agent/tts_out.pcm
100: # ASR result: 你好世界
101: # Sent to agent.
102: ```
103: 
104: 在真实硬件上，`voice_start` 启动麦克风采集线程，实现实时语音交互。
105: 
106: ### 后端扩展
107: 
108: 实现 `voice_tts_ops_t` 或 `voice_asr_ops_t` 接口（`init/synthesize/deinit` 或 `init/recognize/deinit`），在 `voice_channel_init()` 中调用 `register()`，即可通过 CLI 切换。
109: 
110: ## 多节点架构
111: 
112: AI Agent 支持两种多节点协作模式：
113: 
114: ### 模式 A：Node Client（连接到 OpenClaw Gateway）
115: 
116: AI Agent 作为 Node 连接到 OpenClaw Gateway，将本地工具暴露给远程调用。
117: 
118: ```
119: AI Agent (Node) ──WS──▶ OpenClaw Gateway ◀── 其他客户端
120: ```
121: 
122: ```bash
123: vela> set_gateway <gateway_host> <port> <token>
124: vela> node_start
125: ```
126: 
127: ### 模式 B：Hub / Node Manager（接受 Node 连接）
128: 
129: AI Agent 作为 Hub，接受其他 Node 设备连接，动态注册远程工具。
130: 
131: ```
132: Node A (手表) ──WS──▶ AI Agent (Hub) ◀──WS── Node B (音箱)
133: ```
134: 
135: Hub 监听端口 28789，Node 连接后自动发现并注册工具。
136: 
137: ```bash
138: # 查看已连接的 Node
139: vela> node_list
140: 
141: # 断开 Node 连接
142: vela> node_stop
143: ```
144: 
145: ## 音乐播放
146: 
147: Agent 通过内置音乐工具控制播放，支持 PCM/WAV/MP3 格式：
148: 
149: ```bash
150: vela> ask 播放一下 /data/test.pcm
151: vela> ask 暂停
152: vela> ask 把音量调到 80
153: vela> ask 从第 5 秒开始播放 /data/music.wav
154: ```
155:

---

### 一、核心思想

**协作式**：任务主动让出 CPU（不会被强制打断）

**时间片**：按时间分配任务执行机会

**轮询**：主循环不断检查"时间到了没"

---

### 二、最简单的模型

```c
while (1) {
    if (该执行任务A了) 执行任务A();
    if (该执行任务B了) 执行任务B();
    if (该执行任务C了) 执行任务C();
}
```

就像一个**永不停止的传送带**，任务按顺序上去执行。

---

### 三、时间管理原理

#### 3.1 系统时钟

```c
// STM32 的 HAL 库提供一个毫秒计数器
uint32_t HAL_GetTick();  // 返回系统启动后的毫秒数
// 0, 1, 2, 3, ... 一直往上加
```

#### 3.2 判断"时间到了"

```c
// 记录上次执行时间
uint32_t last_time = 0;

while (1) {
    uint32_t now = HAL_GetTick();
    
    // 检查是否过了 10ms
    if (now - last_time >= 10) {
        last_time = now;  // 更新时间戳
        DoSomething();    // 执行任务
    }
}
```

#### 3.3 为什么用 `now - last_time >= 10`？

**防止溢出问题**：

```c
// 假设计数器是 uint32_t，最大值 4294967295
// 当 now=10, last_time=4294967290 时
// now - last_time = 10 - 4294967290 = 16（无符号溢出，结果正确！）

// 如果用 now > last_time + 10
// last_time + 10 会溢出，判断出错！
```

---

### 四、完整调度框架

```c

# Investigation Report: openvela AI Agent + LVGL UI

## Q1. What is `lvgl_ui_channel.c`?

**Purpose:** A *message channel + chat-bubble screen* for the AI agent — chat list, PTT button, recording indicator, close button, on a 466x466 round screen (`lvgl_ui_channel.c:17-24`, `48-58`). It is **not** a display driver and does **not** own `/dev/fb0`.

**Explicit non-ownership:**
- "Do NOT call `lv_init()` — the system (miwear) already initialized LVGL and owns the display + event loop" (`lvgl_ui_channel.c:195-197`)
- "Do NOT create a display or allocate a display buffer... Creating a second display causes resource conflicts and framebuffer contention" (`lvgl_ui_channel.c:199-201`)
- No dedicated thread; relies on miwear's event loop calling `lv_timer_handler()` (`lvgl_ui_channel.c:354-375`, `860-861`)
- `start()` only flips a `running` flag; `init()` only creates widgets on the existing instance (`lvgl_ui_channel.c:183-330`, `354-375`)

**Compiled into current firmware? NO.**
- `# CONFIG_AI_AGENT_LVGL_UI is not set` — `cmake_out\aos_evb_ap\.config:4295`
- Source is only added when the symbol is set — `CMakeLists.txt:101-103`; Kconfig default `n` (`Kconfig:96-99`)
- `.config` has `CONFIG_EXAMPLES_AI_AGENT_VELA=y` (`:4285`) but LVGL UI off.

**Conflict with `zhaoxi_ui`? YES — if enabled.**
- `zhaoxi_ui` calls `lv_init()` + `lv_nuttx_init()` itself and runs its own `while(1) lv_timer_handler()` loop (`zhaoxi_ui.c:297-346`), and bails out if LVGL is already initialized (`zhaoxi_ui.c:288-291`).
- `lvgl_ui_channel` *assumes* an external system (miwear) owns LVGL and loads its screen into the active display (`lvgl_ui_channel.c:195-201`, `526-531`). Two independent LVGL owners is exactly the failure mode the contest already hit: the boot patch says "lvgldemo running concurrently breaks touch input (dual LVGL task conflict)" (`patches\0004-vendor_bes-boot-into-zhaoxi_ui.patch:6-8`).
- Verdict: enabling `CONFIG_AI_AGENT_LVGL_UI` on this firmware would create a **dual-LVGL-owner conflict** with `zhaoxi_ui` (both try to load screens/run timers). It is currently disabled, so **no conflict today**.

## Q2. Exact API to inject a typed string

**The only injection API is the in-process message bus:**
```c
int message_bus_push_inbound(const agent_msg_t *msg);   // message_bus.h:57, message_bus.c:211
```
`agent_msg_t` (`message_bus.h:34-39`):
```c
typedef struct {
    char  channel[16];
    char  chat_id[64];
    char *content;      // heap-allocated; bus takes ownership on success
    char *image_b64;
} agent_msg_t;
```

**Cleanest model to copy — `cmd_ask` (`nsh_commands.c:574-597`):**
```c
agent_msg_t msg = { 0 };
strncpy(msg.channel, "cli", sizeof(msg.channel) - 1);   // :590
strncpy(msg.chat_id, "console", sizeof(msg.chat_id) - 1); // :591
msg.content = strdup(content);                          // :592
message_bus_push_inbound(&msg);                         // :594
```
The agent loop blocks on `message_bus_pop_inbound(&msg, UINT32_MAX)` (`agent_loop.c:1456-1458`), then dispatches. `lvgl_ui_channel.c:750-766` shows the same pattern with `channel="lvgl_ui"`.

**Cross-process caveat (critical):** the bus queues are `static` file-scope objects (`message_bus.c:48-49`), so `message_bus_push_inbound` is only reachable if the caller is linked into the same image/symbol namespace as `ai_agent`. `zhaoxi_ui` links only `lvgl` and its own sources (`zhaoxi_ui\CMakeLists.txt:11-18`) — it does **not** link ai_agent. Under `CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT=y` (`.config:28`) all tasks share one address space, so a direct call is *theoretically* possible if you add the ai_agent include dir + link, but that is **not currently wired** — flag as uncertain/needs build change.

## Q3. Message bus — topics and cross-task mechanism

**Channel/topic identifiers** (`agent_config.h:290-301`): `websocket`, `cli`, `system`, `feishu`, `mqtt`, `weixin`, `quickapp` (if `CONFIG_FEATURE_SYSTEM_VELACLAW`), `lvgl_ui` (if `CONFIG_AI_AGENT_LVGL_UI`); plus `voice` (`:331`).

**Mechanism: in-process only.** Two static ring buffers guarded by pthread mutex+condvar (`message_bus.c:36-51`, `71-148`). No shared memory, no named pipe, no file queue.

**Cross-process options actually available:**
1. **POSIX mqueue bridge** — `/velaclaw_qapp_in`, `/velaclaw_qapp_out`, message format `"chat_id\nquery"` (`agent_main.c:216-219`, `259-278`, `290-320`; client `velaclaw_quickapp_bridge.c:151-197`). **But gated by `CONFIG_FEATURE_SYSTEM_VELACLAW`, which is absent from `.config`** (grep found no match) → **not compiled in this firmware**.
2. **WebSocket server, port 28789** (`AGENT_WS_PORT`, `agent_config.h:224`; `ws_server.c:527-576`). Accepts JSON `{"type":"message","content":"...","chat_id":"..."}` and pushes to inbound (`ws_server.c:440-465`). Only starts after network is up (`agent_main.c:171-172`).
3. **NSH/CLI `ask`** — the current de-facto UI→agent path.
4. **File handoff** — see Q4.

## Q4. How agent output reaches the UI today

`outbound_dispatch_task` routes by channel (`agent_main.c:334-447`):
- `cli` → `printf("\n[Agent]: %s\nvela> ", ...)` to stdout (`agent_main.c:432-437`)
- `feishu`/`websocket`/`mqtt`/`voice`/`lvgl_ui`/`weixin`/`quickapp` each have a branch (`agent_main.c:359-431`)
- Anything else → "Unknown channel" log (`agent_main.c:438-440`)

**No push-to-UI file/socket exists by default for `zhaoxi_ui`.** Existing file-based handoffs:
- **Session transcript:** every turn is appended to `/data/agent/sessions/tg_<chat_id>.jsonl` as `{"role","content","ts"}` (`agent_loop.c:847-848`; `session_mgr.c:54-59`, `124-149`). A UI could tail this file.
- **TASKS.md pattern (the one the contest uses):** the `task-manager` skill writes `/data/agent/TASKS.md` (`skill_loader.c:193`; `agent_skills\task-manager.md:9,17,21`), and `zhaoxi_ui` reads it to count pending items (`zhaoxi_ui.c:32-33`, `79-101`). Note data dir mismatch: firmware `AGENT_DATA_DIR="/data/ai_agent"` (`.config:4289`), while zhaoxi_ui checks `/data/agent` first then falls back to `/data/ai_agent` (`zhaoxi_ui.c:32-33,81-84`).

## Q5. `ask` command trace

1. CLI thread matches `"ask"` → `cmd_ask(argc, argv)` (`nsh_commands.c:976-977`).
2. `cmd_ask` builds `agent_msg_t{channel="cli", chat_id="console", content}` and calls `message_bus_push_inbound` (`nsh_commands.c:589-594`).
3. `agent_loop_task` pops it (`agent_loop.c:1456-1458`), runs slash/NL fast paths, else `run_react_loop(...)` (`agent_loop.c:1495-1556`).
4. `run_react_loop` → **`llm_chat_tools`** (`agent_loop.c:1069`, `1087`, `1187`).

Exact LLM signature (`llm_proxy.h:76-79`):
```c
int llm_chat_tools(const char* system_prompt, cJSON* messages,
                   const char* tools_json, llm_response_t* resp);
```
Non-tool variant: `int llm_chat(const char*, const char*, char*, size_t)` (`llm_proxy.h:48-49`); vision: `llm_chat_vision(...)` (`llm_proxy.h:84-86`).

## Q6. Voice channel

`voice_channel.c` is an **ASR/TTS** channel, not a text-input channel.
- Entry points: `voice_channel_start()` (`voice_channel.c:612`), `voice_channel_stop_with_text(char*, size_t)` (`:861`, decl `voice_channel.h:38`), `voice_channel_test_asr(path)` (`:1198`), `voice_channel_speak(text)` (`voice_channel.h:41`).
- It pushes inbound with `channel=AGENT_CHAN_VOICE`, `chat_id="voice"` (`voice_channel.c:534-543`, `1178-1187`).
- **Cannot accept typed text as input** — text only flows *out* via TTS `speak`. The closest thing is `voice_channel_test_asr`, which reads a **PCM file**, runs ASR, then pushes the recognized text (`voice_channel.c:1153-1196`).
- `voice_channel_stop_with_text` returns ASR text to the caller without pushing (`voice_channel.c:861-899`); the caller (`lvgl_ui_channel`) pushes it itself (`lvgl_ui_channel.c:733-766`).
- So: not the text-input channel the user means. To inject typed text, use `message_bus_push_inbound` directly with any channel (e.g. `"cli"`/`"lvgl_ui"`).

---

## Direct answers

**(a) Does `lvgl_ui_channel.c` conflict with `zhaoxi_ui`?**
Yes, structurally — both assume/own the single LVGL instance. `lvgl_ui_channel` assumes miwear owns LVGL and does not init it (`lvgl_ui_channel.c:195-201`); `zhaoxi_ui` inits LVGL itself and runs its own timer loop (`zhaoxi_ui.c:297-346`). Running both is a dual-LVGL-owner conflict (same class as the documented lvgldemo/zhaoxi conflict, `patches\0004...:6-8`). **However it is NOT compiled in the current firmware** (`# CONFIG_AI_AGENT_LVGL_UI is not set`, `.config:4295`), so there is no conflict today.

**(b) Exact function to inject a typed string into the agent:**
`int message_bus_push_inbound(const agent_msg_t *msg);` (`message_bus.h:57`), with `msg.channel` / `msg.chat_id` set and `msg.content = strdup(text)`. Reference implementation: `cmd_ask` (`nsh_commands.c:589-594`). This is **in-process only**; for the separate `zhaoxi_ui` task the framework's cross-process mqueue bridge exists (`agent_main.c:216-320`) but is **not compiled** (`CONFIG_FEATURE_SYSTEM_VELACLAW` absent), so the practical cross-process route today is the **WebSocket server on port 28789** (`ws_server.c:527-576`) or a **file handoff** (session JSONL / TASKS.md).

**Uncertainty flags:**
- Whether `zhaoxi_ui` can directly link/call `message_bus_push_inbound` in this flat build depends on symbol visibility and link config not present in its CMakeLists — needs a build-level check.
- `CONFIG_FEATURE_SYSTEM_VELACLAW` was searched in `.config`/`config.h` and not found; if it is selected indirectly elsewhere, the mqueue bridge would compile. Direct evidence says disabled.
- Whether enabling `CONFIG_AI_AGENT_LVGL_UI` is intended to run *instead of* `zhaoxi_ui` (not alongside) is not documented.
